title: How this lesson works
text: Before you start · your group ≈ 2 min How this lesson works Slideshow lead Reads each slide aloud and moves the deck forward. Whiteboard scribe Holds the dry erase marker and works problems at the whiteboard. Timekeeper · support Starts each timer and keeps the group on pace. Checker · support Asks "How do we know?" before anyone presses Show answer. Explicit instruction Read it together. Then one person restates it in their own words. Check your understanding Solve alone, compare answers, agree — then press Show answer. Group tasks Start the timer. Everyone contributes before you move on. Exit ticket On your own. Submit it with this lesson's assignment. Day 4 · v–t Graphs & Vectors Antocci Physics · 02 / 30 2 students: lead + timekeeper, scribe + checker. 3 students: third person takes both support duties. Roles rotate at each discussion. Everyone submits their own work.

title: Today's learning target
text: Today's learning target Reasoning R2 Read a v–t graph and split a 2-D velocity into components. Day 4 · v–t Graphs & Vectors Antocci Physics · 03 / 30

title: The asteroid thread
text: The asteroid thread What we know so far Our fictional model uses 8,500 m/s at 15° from the toward-Earth axis. But what does "at 15°" really mean? Today Velocity has COMPONENTS: a part directed toward Earth and a part perpendicular. We need both to predict where it will be. Day 4 · v–t Graphs & Vectors Antocci Physics · 04 / 30

title: What does a velocity–time graph look like?
text: Recap ≈ 5 min Yesterday: the slope of a position–time graph is velocity. What does a velocity–time graph look like for the same motion? Day 4 · v–t Graphs & Vectors Antocci Physics · 05 / 30

title: A flat line can show motion
text: See it → describe it Target R2 A flat line can show motion Read the vertical axis: velocity . The cart keeps moving at +2 m/s. Velocity over time Flat velocity means steady velocity, not necessarily stopped. Day 4 · v–t Graphs & Vectors Antocci Physics · 06 / 30

title: A horizontal line can mean motion
text: Check your understanding Target R2 A horizontal line can mean motion A velocity–time graph stays at +3 m/s for 4 s. Does the object stop? How far does it move? Solve alone · compare as a group · then check. Your turn Work it out on paper. Then press Show answer to check. Day 4 · v–t Graphs & Vectors Antocci Physics · 07 / 30

title: Four seconds of equal steps
text: See it → describe it Target R2 Four seconds of equal steps Each second adds +2 m. Four equal steps give +8 m. Match the motion to the graph This is the motion shown by +2 m/s for 4 s. Day 4 · v–t Graphs & Vectors Antocci Physics · 08 / 30

title: Sketch the v–t graph for yesterday’s walk
text: Velocity–time graphs ≈ 10 min Sketch the v–t graph for yesterday's walks Constant velocity Horizontal line. Changing velocity Sloped or curved line. Coming soon Slope of v–t = acceleration. Day 4 · v–t Graphs & Vectors Antocci Physics · 09 / 30

title: The axis changes the meaning
text: Explicit instruction Target R2 The axis changes the meaning Graph Height tells you Slope tells you Position vs. time Position Velocity Velocity vs. time Velocity Acceleration A line below zero on a velocity graph represents negative velocity. It can be perfectly horizontal while the object keeps moving. Day 4 · v–t Graphs & Vectors Antocci Physics · 10 / 30

title: Read the axis before the line
text: 2026-XJ · The Other Direction · Graphic novel, page 13 Read the axis before the line The velocity–time graph is horizontal at +1 meter per second from zero to four seconds. Mr. Antocci explains that velocity stays constant while Maz points out that the object is still moving. A flat line at +1 m/s means steady motion in the positive direction. How would the same line shape mean something different on a position–time graph? Part 1 · Compare the graph stories · Write your own answer in Work. Fictional story · Original artwork · Day 4

title: Use a rectangle to count change
text: I do · count the area Target R2 Use a rectangle to count change 2 m/s × 4 s = +8 m The area between this velocity line and zero gives displacement. Height × width Height is 2; width is 4. Day 4 · v–t Graphs & Vectors Antocci Physics · 12 / 30

title: Reading before calculating
text: Check your understanding Target R2 Reading before calculating An object has v = −4 m/s from 0 to 3 s, then v = 0 from 3 to 5 s. Describe its motion and find total displacement. Solve alone · compare as a group · then check. Your turn Work it out on paper. Then press Show answer to check. Day 4 · v–t Graphs & Vectors Antocci Physics · 13 / 30

title: A vector is an arrow.
text: Vectors as arrows ≈ 20 min A vector is an arrow. Its length is the magnitude. It points in the direction . Day 4 · v–t Graphs & Vectors Antocci Physics · 14 / 30

title: Draw each velocity vector
text: Practice ≈ 20 min Draw each velocity vector 01 A car going 60 mph east 02 A plane going 200 mph north 03 A runner going 5 m/s southwest Draw Time Day 4 · v–t Graphs & Vectors Antocci Physics · 15 / 30

title: A common scale makes arrows useful
text: 2026-XJ · The Other Direction · Graphic novel, page 14 A common scale makes arrows useful At one square per meter per second, one arrow is four squares east and another is two squares north. Turning an arrow changes velocity even if its length stays the same. Use the same units and scale before comparing arrow lengths. What changes when you rotate an arrow without changing its length? Part 2 · Check the arrow and its components · Write your own answer in Work. Fictional story · Original artwork · Day 4

title: Split the asteroid's velocity
text: 2026-XJ in two parts ≈ 20 min Draw Split the asteroid's velocity Velocity 8,500 m/s at 15° Toward Earth v · cos 15° ≈ 8,210 m/s Perpendicular v · sin 15° ≈ 2,200 m/s Today this is visual. Protractors and graphic decomposition come next lesson. Day 4 · v–t Graphs & Vectors Antocci Physics · 17 / 30

title: What happens below zero?
text: Try it as a group Target R2 Draw What happens below zero? Velocity is −1 m/s for 4 s. How much does position change? Solve alone · compare as a group · then check. Negative velocity Right is positive. Day 4 · v–t Graphs & Vectors Antocci Physics · 18 / 30

title: A velocity vector has two components
text: Explicit instruction Target R2 Draw A velocity vector has two components For a vector in a horizontal plane, choose perpendicular x and y axes. A velocity of +4 m/s east and +3 m/s north is one diagonal motion with both components occurring at once. |v| = √(4² + 3²) = 5 m/s Day 4 · v–t Graphs & Vectors Antocci Physics · 19 / 30

title: One diagonal, two directions
text: See it → describe it Target R2 Draw One diagonal, two directions The arrow reaches 4 m east and 3 m north. Components tell us the separate east and north changes. Read the supplied components Components describe the same displacement. No angle calculation is needed. Day 4 · v–t Graphs & Vectors Antocci Physics · 20 / 30

title: One motion, two components
text: 2026-XJ · The Other Direction · Graphic novel, page 15 One motion, two components The fictional 8,500 meter-per-second vector is fifteen degrees from the toward-Earth axis. Its perpendicular components are about 8,210 meters per second toward Earth and 2,200 meters per second sideways. The perpendicular components describe one simultaneous velocity. Why do 8,210 and 2,200 not add to 8,500 as ordinary numbers? Part 2 · Check the arrow and its components · Write your own answer in Work. Fictional story · Original artwork · Day 4

title: Decompose 2026-XJ's velocity
text: On graph paper ≈ 13 min Decompose 2026-XJ's velocity 01 Draw the velocity vector to scale. 02 Draw its toward-Earth component. 03 Draw its perpendicular component. 04 In 6 months, how far does each component move it? Use rate × time. Work Time Day 4 · v–t Graphs & Vectors Antocci Physics · 22 / 30

title: A model with limits
text: Back to 2026-XJ ≈ 13 min Work This simplified model assumes constant velocity. A real trajectory also changes under gravity. Day 4 · v–t Graphs & Vectors Antocci Physics · 23 / 30

title: The angle needs a reference axis
text: Explicit instruction Target R2 Work The angle needs a reference axis Let θ be measured counterclockwise from the positive x-axis. v x = v cos θ v y = v sin θ Adjacent component uses cosine. Opposite component uses sine. Use degree mode for an angle in degrees. Day 4 · v–t Graphs & Vectors Antocci Physics · 24 / 30

title: Read components, not an angle
text: Try it as a group Target R2 Work Read components, not an angle A displacement has components 2 m east and 1 m north. Where is the endpoint relative to the start? Solve alone · compare as a group · then check. Two directions Follow each component. Day 4 · v–t Graphs & Vectors Antocci Physics · 25 / 30

title: A clearly defined asteroid vector
text: Worked example Target R2 Work A clearly defined asteroid vector Teaching convention: +x points from the initial asteroid position toward Earth. +y is perpendicular in the diagram plane. The velocity points 15° from +x toward +y. v x = 8,500 cos 15° ≈ +8,210 m/s v y = 8,500 sin 15° ≈ +2,200 m/s Day 4 · v–t Graphs & Vectors Antocci Physics · 26 / 30

title: A smaller component still matters
text: 2026-XJ · The Other Direction · Graphic novel, page 16 A smaller component still matters Over 1.6 times ten to the seventh seconds, the constant-velocity model gives about 131 million kilometers toward Earth and 35 million kilometers sideways. Mr. Antocci calls this a model rather than an orbit forecast. Over six months, even the smaller sideways rate produces a large displacement. What information is still missing before you can locate the final position? Part 3 · Challenge the six-month prediction · Write your own answer in Work. Fictional story · Original artwork · Day 4

title: Your turn: velocity and time
text: Try it yourself Target R2 Your turn: velocity and time Velocity is +3 m/s for 2 s. Find displacement and name the direction. Solve alone · compare as a group · then check. Velocity over time Right is positive. Day 4 · v–t Graphs & Vectors Antocci Physics · 28 / 30

title: Name the graph before reading it
text: Check a common mix-up Target R2 Name the graph before reading it A flat position graph means stopped. A flat velocity graph means velocity is constant. A path through the problem 01 First Read the vertical-axis label. 02 Then Say what stays the same. Read one step at a time. Day 4 · v–t Graphs & Vectors Antocci Physics · 29 / 30
